# Redirect to a URL from HTTP request data (C#)

`qualor:csharp/open-redirect` · Issue · Severity: Medium · [CWE-601](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A01:2025 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/), [A01:2021 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data in ASP.NET Core (MVC and Web API controllers, Minimal APIs, Razor Pages) that
decides where the response sends the browser:

- the URL given to a controller's or page's `Redirect`, `RedirectPermanent`,
  `RedirectPreserveMethod` and `RedirectPermanentPreserveMethod`, to `new RedirectResult(...)`, to
  `Results.Redirect` and `TypedResults.Redirect`, and to `HttpResponse.Redirect`;
- the `Location` header set by hand (`Response.Headers.Location`, the indexer, `Append` or `Add`
  with `"Location"` or `HeaderNames.Location`).

A URL is reported when request data can set its scheme or host: the value used as it is, or put
after `"/"`, `"~/"`, a scheme, or a host without a separator (`"https://shop.example" + path`).
Request data after a fixed path or origin and a separator (`"/orders/" + id`,
`"https://help.example/articles/" + id`), in the query (`"/search?q=" + q`,
`QueryHelpers.AddQueryString("/login", ...)`), percent-encoded with `Uri.EscapeDataString`, after
the application's `Request.PathBase`, or checked first with `Url.IsLocalUrl` or Duende
IdentityServer's interaction service (`IsValidReturnUrl`, or a non-null
`GetAuthorizationContextAsync` result), is not reported. Neither is a URL rebuilt on the request's
own host (`"https://" + Request.Host + Request.Path`, the interpolated form,
`UriHelper.BuildAbsolute("https", Request.Host, ...)`). `LocalRedirect` and `Results.LocalRedirect`
are never reported: they refuse URLs that are not local.

Request data means the parameters of controller actions, Razor Pages handlers and Minimal API
handlers (strings, string arrays, `StringValues`, forms, uploaded files, the body stream, and any
parameter bound with `[FromQuery]`, `[FromRoute]`, `[FromForm]`, `[FromHeader]`, `[FromBody]` or
`[AsParameters]`), `[BindProperty]` properties, and the request object itself (`Request.Query`,
`Form`, `Headers`, `Cookies`, `RouteValues`, `Path`, ...).
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
A link to your own site that forwards the visitor to any address is a gift for phishing: the
link looks trustworthy, and after signing in the user lands on a copy of your login page that
collects their password. The `returnUrl` of a login page is the classic case. Browsers also treat
`//evil.example` and `/\evil.example` as another host, so a value that only looks like a path can
still leave your site.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** after signing in, the user is sent to whatever `returnUrl` says.

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

public class AccountController : Controller
{
    [HttpGet]
    public IActionResult SignedIn(string returnUrl)
    {
        return Redirect(returnUrl);
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** `LocalRedirect` only follows URLs on this site.

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

public class AccountController : Controller
{
    [HttpGet]
    public IActionResult SignedIn(string returnUrl)
    {
        return LocalRedirect(returnUrl);
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Use `LocalRedirect` (MVC, Razor Pages) or `Results.LocalRedirect` (Minimal APIs) for return
  URLs: it throws for a URL that is not local.
- Or check the URL with `Url.IsLocalUrl` (or `RedirectHttpResult.IsLocalUrl`) and fall back to a
  fixed page when it fails.
- Build other targets from a fixed path or origin and put request data only after a separator or
  in the query, or redirect with `RedirectToAction` and `RedirectToPage`, which generate URLs of
  this site.
- If users may choose an external site, map their choice to an allow-list of known URLs.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- ASP.NET Core MVC and Web API
- ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs
- ASP.NET Core Razor Pages

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Taint is followed through the methods of one file, not into other files. Request data read
  inside an expression-bodied method (`=> ...`) or a property getter is missed.
- Minimal APIs: a class or record parameter bound from the JSON body without `[FromBody]` is not
  taken for request data, and a handler that is a method of another class is missed. A controller
  named `*Controller` whose base class has another name is missed.
- An enum parameter is reported when the enum is declared after its use or in another file. Only
  allow-lists written as `static readonly` tables of literals count; an equality check or
  `Enumerable.Contains(...)` called as a static method does not, and a variable assigned again
  after a check still counts as checked.
- `Url.IsLocalUrl` (and IdentityServer's `IsValidReturnUrl`) counts when it is the condition of an
  `if` (alone or with `&&`, or negated with a branch that leaves the method or sets a fixed URL)
  or of a ternary, and so does a null check of IdentityServer's `GetAuthorizationContextAsync`
  result; a result stored in a variable first, or a check in a helper method, is not recognised.
- A check of the URL's host against an allow-list is not recognised: the URL is still reported
  after it.
- `Request.PathBase` is taken for the application's configured path base and is not reported.
- A URL rebuilt on the request's own host is recognised only when it is written in place as
  scheme, `Request.Host` and then only `PathBase`, `Path` and `QueryString` (or with
  `UriHelper.BuildAbsolute` with a literal `"https"` or `Request.Scheme` as its scheme); built in
  steps, or with a scheme taken from request data, it is still reported.
- The value of `Uri.MakeRelativeUri` is not reported, also when its argument is a URL from the
  request.
- The value of an awaited `GetXxx`, `FindXxx` or `LoadXxx` call on another object (a record found
  by an id) is taken for stored data, so a URL saved in it is not reported; such a method that only
  hands request data back is missed. Without `await`, the looked-up value still counts as request
  data.
- An object returned by a helper method counts as request data as a whole when one of its fields
  holds request data, so a checked URL in another of its fields is still reported.
- A fixed path or origin is recognised when it is written in place as the first part of the URL;
  one held in a constant or read from configuration is not, so request data after it is still
  reported.
- `Response.Redirect` and the `Location` header are checked on `Response`, `HttpContext.Response`,
  a `context.Response` and an `HttpResponse` parameter or variable; a response reached otherwise
  is missed. The `Refresh` header and `AuthenticationProperties.RedirectUri` are not checked.
- OpenGrep 1.30 does not parse some newer C# syntax (raw strings with `$$"""`, types declared
  without a body such as `class X : Y;`, some multi-line collection expressions); code in those
  parts of a file may be missed.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/csharp/redirect/open-redirect.cs`](../../../rules/csharp/redirect/open-redirect.cs) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/csharp/redirect/open-redirect.yml`](../../../rules/csharp/redirect/open-redirect.yml), added in version 2026.10.5.
